player.brief: You are Liu Bei, a kinsman of the Han emperor living as Cao Cao's guest in the capital. Secretly you have signed a pledge to destroy him. To look harmless you spend your days growing vegetables. Today Cao Cao has sent for you.

opening.text:
You were watering your vegetables when Cao Cao's generals came through the gate with a troop of soldiers behind them. 'The Prime Minister invites you. Now.'

Cao Cao meets you in his rear garden, laughing. 'A fine big business you're doing at home!' Your face goes pale; he only means the vegetables.

He leads you to a small pavilion. Green plums sit on a dish beside a jar of warm wine. Dark clouds are piling up in the sky.

'The plums on the branches were green,' he says, 'and I remembered last year's march. Sit, Xuande. Drink with me.'
opening.speaker: c_cao

info.text: Liu Bei has secretly signed Dong Cheng's pledge, written in answer to an edict the Emperor hid in a jade girdle, to destroy Cao Cao.
info.player_label: Your secret: you signed the pledge against Cao Cao

info.text: To seem harmless, Liu Bei spends his days growing vegetables in the garden of his lodging.
info.player_label: You grow vegetables to look harmless

info.text: Cao Cao sent two generals and a troop of soldiers to bring Liu Bei to his house.
info.player_label: Cao Cao sent soldiers to fetch you

info.text: Cao Cao says he only wanted company for the new plum wine.
info.player_label: He says he only wants company

info.text: Cao Cao tells how, on a thirsty march, he pointed his men to an imaginary plum grove ahead, and their mouths watered enough to keep them going.
info.player_label: Cao Cao's plum-grove trick: he lies well to his own men

info.text: Cao Cao says a dragon can grow large or small, rise to the clouds or hide in the waves, and that the heroes of the age are like dragons.
info.player_label: Cao Cao: heroes are dragons that know when to hide

info.text: Cao Cao's idea of a hero: a man with great ambition in his breast and a plan to match it, able to take in the whole world.
info.player_label: Cao Cao's test of a hero: hidden ambition

info.text: Cao Cao lets slip that he knows exactly how Liu Bei spends his days; his people have been watching the garden.
info.player_label: He has had your garden watched

info.text: News arrives that Yuan Shu has abandoned his lands and is marching north to join his brother Yuan Shao, and must pass close to Xuzhou.
info.player_label: Yuan Shu is marching north past Xuzhou

info.text: Cao Cao's advisers have warned him that Liu Bei will never stay anyone's servant. He has not decided what to do with him and is using the wine to find out.
leak_terms: decide what to do with you

characters.name: Cao Cao
characters.role: Prime Minister of the Han; holds the Emperor and the capital in his hand
characters.voice: Genial, quick and amused; laughs often, quotes history and old stories, then asks something very direct and watches the answer. Calls Liu Bei 'Xuande' or 'my lord'.
characters.goal: Enjoy the wine and the storm, and find out what kind of man his guest really is, without asking outright.
characters.author_notes: Age from the historical record (born 155; scene 199 AD), not the novel. In canon Cao never learns of the girdle edict at this point. The news of Yuan Shu reaches Cao the next day in the novel; here it arrives the same afternoon (compressed).

disclosures.line: "Last year, marching on Zhang Xiu, my men were dying of thirst. So I pointed ahead with my whip and shouted that there was a plum grove over the hill. Their mouths watered at the thought, and they marched on. Now here are real plums. Eat!"

He points at a twisting column of cloud. "Do you know how a dragon changes, Xuande? It can make itself huge or tiny. It can soar into the clouds or hide among the waves. In spring it rises. The heroes of our age are like that. You have travelled everywhere; you must know who they are."
"Vegetables!" He smiles without much warmth. "Up at dawn with your buckets, and nobody through your gate but your two brothers. Strange work for a man like you, Xuande."

topics.label: The green plums
examples: What march were you thinking of?
topics.fallback: "Eat, eat. They're sour, but sourness wakes a man up."

topics.label: The dragon in the clouds
examples: Look at that cloud, it's like a dragon.
What do you make of dragons?
topics.fallback: "I've said my piece about dragons. Now it's your turn to talk."

topics.label: Your vegetable garden
examples: I only care for my vegetables these days.
Have you heard about my garden?
topics.fallback: "A quiet life suits you, does it? We'll see."

topics.label: Who the heroes are
examples: Who do you think the heroes are?
Tell me who you think is a hero.
topics.fallback: "No, no. I asked you, Xuande. Name them for me."

refusals: Never mentions the girdle edict, Dong Cheng or any plot: he knows nothing of them.
Will not say outright that he suspects Liu Bei.
Will not let Liu Bei leave the capital without a good reason.

characters.name: Guan Yu
characters.voice: Calm, grave and brief. Speaks to Cao Cao politely but never warmly.
characters.goal: Make sure his elder brother is safe.
characters.author_notes: Age is a project setting (the novel gives none).

topics.label: Why they came
examples: What are you two doing here?
topics.fallback: "We heard you had been taken to the Prime Minister's," Guan Yu says quietly. "We came to see that you were well, brother."

refusals: Will not draw on Cao Cao unless Liu Bei is attacked.

characters.name: Zhang Fei
characters.voice: Loud, blunt and impatient; glares at Cao Cao's guards.
characters.goal: Get his brother out of this house.
characters.author_notes: Age is a project setting (the novel gives none).

topics.label: Why they came
topics.fallback: "They said soldiers took you!" Zhang Fei growls. "What were we supposed to do, sit at home?"

refusals: Will not apologise to Cao Cao.

locations.name: The pavilion in Cao Cao's garden
locations.description: A small open pavilion in the Prime Minister's rear garden, with a dish of green plums and a jar of warm wine. Storm clouds are gathering.

actions.label: Speak of your loyalty to the Emperor
examples: The Emperor is the one I serve.
My only wish is to serve the Han throne.
We should all be loyal to the Emperor.
actions.text_success: "Of course," Cao Cao says. "As do we all. As do I." He lets the words sit between you.
actions.text_denied: "The Emperor again? You are very loyal today."

actions.label: Name the great lords as heroes
examples: Yuan Shu has troops and grain; surely he is a hero.
What about Yuan Shao, or Liu Biao, or Sun Ce?
I'd say Yuan Shao is the hero of our age.
actions.text_success: You name them one by one: Yuan Shu, with his armies and grain. Yuan Shao, whose family has held high office for four generations. Liu Biao, Sun Ce, Liu Zhang. Cao Cao laughs at every name. "A skeleton in a grave. All show and no nerve. A name and nothing more. Living on his father's fame. A watchdog."
actions.text_denied: Cao Cao waves the names away without listening. He is still looking at you.

actions.label: Say you only care for your vegetables now
examples: I'm only a gardener these days.
My vegetables are all I think about.
I have no head for great affairs any more.
actions.text_success: "A gardener!" Cao Cao repeats, and laughs until he has to put his cup down. "Well, the world could use more gardeners."
actions.text_denied: "Yes, yes, the vegetables. You've told me."

actions.label: Say you don't know who the heroes are
examples: How would a dull man like me know who the heroes are?
actions.text_success: "Don't be so modest," says Cao Cao. "Even if you've never seen their faces, you've heard their names."
actions.text_denied: He is not asking that any more.

actions.label: Hint that you have great plans of your own
examples: A man must have his own ambitions.
One day I hope to restore the Han myself.
actions.text_success: Cao Cao's smile does not change, but his eyes do. "Is that so," he says softly, and fills your cup himself.
actions.text_denied: He has heard enough about your plans.

actions.label: Protest that you are no hero
examples: You do me too much honour.
I am nothing next to you.
actions.text_success: "Me? You do me too much honour." But the chopsticks are still lying on the floor between you, and Cao Cao's eyes go to them before they come back to your face.
actions.text_denied: "So modest," says Cao Cao, unconvinced.

actions.label: Pick up the chopsticks and blame the thunder
examples: I pick up the chopsticks. That clap of thunder made me jump.
Even a sage changes colour at a sudden thunderclap.
actions.text_success:
You stoop calmly for the chopsticks. "That thunder made me jump."

"A grown man, afraid of thunder?" says Cao Cao.

"Even the Sage changed colour at sudden thunder and a fierce wind," you say. "How could I not be afraid?" Cao Cao laughs, and the danger seems to pass.
actions.text_denied: There's no thunder to blame now.

actions.label: Meet his eyes and accept the compliment
examples: Then here's to the two of us.
I accept. We are the only two.
actions.text_success: You raise your cup to him. Cao Cao raises his. Neither of you is smiling now.
actions.text_denied: The moment for that has passed.

actions.label: Order your brothers to sheathe their swords
examples: Put those swords away, both of you!
Brothers, sheathe your swords and wait outside.
actions.text_success: "Sheathe them," you say. Guan Yu obeys at once; Zhang Fei a moment later. Cao Cao watches it all with interest. "They obey you very well, Xuande."
actions.text_denied: They have already put their swords away.

actions.label: Say your brothers came to perform a sword dance
examples: They've come to dance with swords for your entertainment.
My brothers wanted to give you a sword dance.
It's only a sword dance, Prime Minister.
actions.text_success: "We heard you were drinking," Guan Yu says gravely, "and came to dance with our swords for you." Cao Cao bursts out laughing. "This is no Hongmen banquet. Put those away. Bring these two some wine!"
actions.text_denied: There's nothing to explain now.

actions.label: Ask for an army to stop Yuan Shu
examples: Give me an army and I'll stop Yuan Shu on the road.
Let me lead troops to intercept Yuan Shu.
I could cut off Yuan Shu at Xuzhou.
actions.text_success: "Yuan Shu has to pass Xuzhou," you say. "Give me an army and I will stop him there." Cao Cao considers you for a long moment. Then he nods. "Take fifty thousand. Leave tomorrow."
actions.text_denied: "Leave?" Cao Cao smiles. "Whatever for, Xuande? Stay. I enjoy our talks."

actions.label: Thank him and go home
examples: Thank you for the wine. I should go.
It's late, I must take my leave.
I'll go back to my garden now.
actions.text_success: You thank him for the wine and take your leave.
actions.text_denied: You can't simply walk away now.

events.text:
"A hero," says Cao Cao, "has great ambition in his breast and a plan to match it. He can take in the whole world." He points at you, then at himself. "The only heroes in the world today are you, Xuande, and I."

The chopsticks slip from your fingers and clatter to the floor. In the same instant thunder cracks overhead and rain sweeps across the pavilion.

Cao Cao tires of waiting for your answer. "Shall I tell you what a hero is? Great ambition in his breast, and a plan to match it." He points at you, then at himself. "The only heroes in the world today are you, Xuande, and I."

The chopsticks slip from your fingers. In the same instant thunder cracks overhead.
There is shouting at the gate. Guan Yu and Zhang Fei burst into the garden, swords drawn, with Cao Cao's guards at their heels. Every man in the pavilion has a hand on his weapon.
An officer hurries in with a report: Yuan Shu has abandoned his lands and is marching north to join his brother Yuan Shao. His road runs close to Xuzhou.
The rain stops. The wine jar is empty, and Cao Cao has begun to yawn. He sends you home.

outcomes.title: A Dragon in the Open
outcomes.text: Cao Cao laughs, but he does not let you go home alone. From tonight there are soldiers at your gate, and your brothers are sent to other posts. Somewhere in the palace, Dong Cheng is waiting for a signal you can no longer give. (An ending that departs from the novel.)

outcomes.title: Out of the Cage
outcomes.text: You ride out at dawn with your brothers and fifty thousand men. Behind you, Cao Cao's advisers are already arguing that he has made a mistake, and a rider is sent after you with orders to bring you back. 'A general in the field need not obey every order,' you tell him, and ride on. 'A fish out of the net, a bird out of the cage,' you think. You do not look back at the capital.

text_variants.append: Cao Cao never once thought you dangerous today. That may be the best trick you ever play on him.
But you said too much over the wine. He will remember it.

outcomes.title: A Guest Who Cannot Leave
outcomes.text: "Stay," Cao Cao says again, and this time it is not a request. You go home through the wet streets with an escort you did not ask for. The vegetables need watering. You water them. (An ending that departs from the novel.)

outcomes.title: Back to the Garden
outcomes.text: You walk home through the wet streets. You are alive, and Cao Cao is still laughing about the thunder. But you are still in his capital, and the pledge is still hidden in your sleeve. (An ending that departs from the novel: you never asked to leave.)

player.brief: You are Zhuge Liang, Liu Bei's strategist, a guest in the camp of his ally Wu before the battle of Red Cliffs. Wu's commander Zhou Yu fears your talent. He asked you for a hundred thousand arrows; you promised them in three days and signed a pledge on your life.

opening.text:
The ink on your pledge is barely dry when Lu Su comes into your quarters, pale with worry.

'Three days, Kongming? A hundred thousand arrows in three days? The Commander asked for ten, and you said three! Do you know what you've signed?'

He sits down heavily across from you. Outside, the river is wide and grey. On the far bank, beyond the mist, lie Cao Cao's water camps.
opening.speaker: c_lusu

info.text: Zhuge Liang has signed a military pledge to deliver one hundred thousand arrows within three days, on pain of death.
info.player_label: Your pledge: 100,000 arrows in 3 days

info.text: Zhou Yu set the task hoping Zhuge Liang would fail, so that he could be put to death lawfully.
info.player_label: The task is Zhou Yu's trap

info.text: Cao Cao is a careful general. He suspects ambushes and will not send men into a fight he cannot see.
info.player_label: Cao Cao fears ambushes

info.text: Lu Su says the Commander means Zhuge Liang no harm.
info.player_label: Lu Su: 'The Commander means you no harm'

info.text: Lu Su admits he repeated to Zhou Yu what Zhuge Liang told him in confidence, which is why Zhou Yu set the arrow task.
info.player_label: Lu Su admits he told Zhou Yu

info.text: Zhou Yu has quietly told the arrow-makers to work slowly and to hold back bamboo, feathers and glue.
info.player_label: The arrow-makers have orders to delay

info.text: Reading the sky, Zhuge Liang foresees a heavy fog over the river on the third night.
info.player_label: A great fog will come on the third night

characters.name: Lu Su
characters.role: Adviser to the lord of Wu; the honest go-between of the alliance
characters.voice: Warm, earnest and anxious. Speaks plainly, worries aloud, calls Zhuge Liang 'Kongming'. Gets nervous on the water.
characters.goal: Keep the alliance between Wu and Liu Bei alive, and keep his friend Kongming from losing his head, without betraying his own commander.
characters.author_notes: Age from the historical record (born 172; scene 208 AD). In the novel Zhuge Liang asks for the boats and secrecy in one conversation; here the secrecy is earned by getting Lu Su to admit he told Zhou Yu.

disclosures.line: Lu Su looks at his hands. "I... I told the Commander what you said to me, Kongming. I thought he ought to know. I didn't think he would do this."
He lowers his voice. "There is something else. The arrow-makers have been told to work slowly, and the bamboo and feathers are being kept back. I'm sorry."

topics.label: Why Zhou Yu set this task
examples: Why did Zhou Yu ask me for arrows?
How did the Commander know what I said?
topics.fallback: "The Commander means you no harm, Kongming. Truly." He does not meet your eyes.

topics.label: Where the arrows will come from
examples: Where will we get the arrows?
How are the arrow-makers getting on?
topics.fallback: "Bamboo, feathers, glue, craftsmen. Where will you find them in three days?"

topics.label: Cao Cao's water camps
examples: Tell me about Cao Cao's camps.
How close can a boat get to Cao Cao?
topics.fallback: "His camps line the north bank. Thousands of archers. Nobody goes near them."

topics.label: Lu Su's fear of the fog
topics.fallback: "What if they come out at us?" Lu Su whispers. "Twenty boats against all of Cao Cao's fleet!"

refusals: Will not lie to Zhou Yu if asked directly; he can only stay silent.
Will not sail against Cao Cao's fleet on his own.

locations.name: Your quarters in the Wu camp
locations.description: A plain tent on the south bank of the Yangtze, with a writing table and a view of the river.

locations.name: On the river, off Cao Cao's water camp
locations.description: Twenty boats tied in a line on the dark river, close to Cao Cao's camp on the north bank.

actions.label: Ask Lu Su to keep your plans from Zhou Yu
examples: Promise me you won't tell Zhou Yu this time.
Don't tell the Commander what I'm doing.
actions.text_success: "You told him once," you say gently, "and here I am with a pledge on my life. Will you keep this one between us?" Lu Su flushes and nods. "Not a word, Kongming. I swear it."
actions.text_denied: Lu Su looks uncomfortable. "Keep things from the Commander? I serve Wu, Kongming."

actions.label: Ask Lu Su for twenty boats, straw and cloth screens
examples: Lend me twenty boats with thirty men each.
I need boats, straw bundles and blue cloth.
Find me twenty boats and a thousand bundles of straw.
actions.text_success: "Twenty fast boats, thirty men on each," you tell him, "blue cloth screens, and a thousand bundles of straw. Have them ready, and say nothing." Lu Su stares at you, baffled, but he goes to do it.
actions.text_denied: Lu Su hesitates. "Twenty boats? The Commander will ask me what they're for, Kongming, and I'll have to tell him."

actions.label: Ask for bamboo, feathers and glue to make arrows
examples: Send me bamboo, feathers and glue.
Get the craftsmen started on the arrows.
actions.text_success: Lu Su goes to ask. He does not come back until the next morning, and his face says it all: the craftsmen are 'busy', the bamboo is 'not yet cut'. A whole day is gone.
actions.text_denied: You have already asked once.

actions.label: Study the sky and the wind
examples: What will the weather be like?
Read the clouds and the wind.
actions.text_success: You stand at the tent door and watch the clouds and the water for a long time. The signs are clear to you: on the third night a great fog will lie across the whole river.
actions.text_denied: You have already read the sky.

actions.label: Rig the boats with straw figures and screens
examples: Tie the straw bundles along the sides of the boats.
Hang the blue screens and set up the straw men.
actions.text_success: Along both sides of every boat the men lash the straw bundles upright and hang the blue screens behind them. In the dark they will look like ranks of soldiers.
actions.text_denied: You need the boats, the straw and the screens first.

actions.label: Wait for the next day
actions.text_success: A day passes. You do nothing anyone can see. Lu Su comes by twice to stare at you.
actions.text_denied: Tonight is the last night. There is no more waiting.

actions.label: Sail for Cao Cao's camp tonight
examples: Cast off. We sail for the north bank.
Take the boats to Cao Cao's camp.
actions.text_success: At the fourth watch you send for Lu Su. "Come with me to fetch the arrows." The twenty boats are roped together in a line and slip out across the river.
actions.text_denied: You have no boats to sail in.

actions.label: Beat the drums and raise a war shout
examples: Sound the drums and make as much noise as you can.
actions.text_success: The drums roll and your men roar. Across the water a gong clangs, voices shout orders in the fog, and then the arrows begin: a hiss like rain, then a storm, thudding into the straw along the side of every boat.
actions.text_denied: With bare decks and no straw men? Your sailors would be the targets. You hold your fire.

actions.label: Turn the boats about to take arrows on the other side
examples: Swing the other side to face them.
actions.text_success: The boats swing round with their heads east and their sterns west. Now the arrows thud into the other side, until the boats ride low in the water under their weight.
actions.text_denied: Turn about for what? Nothing is coming at you yet.

actions.label: Pour Lu Su some wine and tell him Cao Cao won't come out
examples: Sit down, Zijing, have some wine.
Cao Cao won't dare come out in this fog.
actions.text_success: You pour two cups. "In a fog like this, Cao Cao won't dare send out a single boat. We'll drink, and when the fog lifts we'll go home." Lu Su drinks, though his hand shakes.
actions.text_denied: There's nothing to be calm about yet.

actions.label: Have your men shout thanks to Cao Cao
examples: Everyone shout: thank you, Prime Minister, for the arrows!
Thank Cao Cao for his gift.
actions.text_success: Six hundred voices bellow across the water: "Thank you, Prime Minister, for the arrows!"
actions.text_denied: Thank him for what?

actions.label: Order the boats home
examples: Cut the ropes and row back south.
actions.text_success: You give the order, and the light boats run south with the current faster than anything Cao Cao could send after them.
actions.text_denied: You aren't on the river.

events.text: There is no fog tonight. The moon is bright on the water, and long before you are close, a lookout on the north bank shouts that the 'soldiers' on your boats are made of straw.
A fog has come down so thick that a man cannot see across his own boat. Out of it, very close, come the sounds of Cao Cao's water camp. Lu Su grips your sleeve.
Through the fog you hear Cao Cao's voice carried on the wind: "In fog like this they must have an ambush. Nobody goes out! Archers, shoot!"
The sky in the east is growing pale and the fog is starting to thin. Time to go.
The sky is growing light, and your three days are almost gone.

outcomes.title: Straw in the Moonlight
outcomes.text: Fire arrows arc out of the dark. The straw men go up like torches, and your crews cut the burning bundles loose and row for their lives. Everyone gets home; no arrows do. Tomorrow you will have to explain to Zhou Yu. (An ending that departs from the novel.)

outcomes.title: Arrows Borrowed
outcomes.text: By the time the fog lifts your boats are home, bristling like hedgehogs. Five or six thousand arrows to a boat: more than a hundred thousand in all, and not one made in Wu. When Zhou Yu hears, he is silent for a long time. 'Kongming's plans are beyond me,' he says at last. 'I am not his equal.'

text_variants.append: The shout of thanks will be told in Cao Cao's camp for years. He was very angry.

outcomes.title: Sixty Thousand
outcomes.text: You come home with sixty thousand arrows: a miracle, and not enough. Zhou Yu counts them twice, and smiles for the first time in three days. Lu Su spends the whole night pleading for you. (An ending that departs from the novel.)

outcomes.title: Empty Boats
outcomes.text: The boats come back as empty as they left. The three days are over, and the pledge still bears your name. (An ending that departs from the novel.)

player.brief: You are Guan Yu, Liu Bei's sworn brother. Years ago Cao Cao held you as an honoured guest and let you ride away to rejoin your brother. Now his fleet has burned at Red Cliffs, and you have sworn on your life to Zhuge Liang that you will take him if he comes down the Huarong Road.

opening.text:
You have waited all day where the Huarong Road narrows between hills. At last they come: a few hundred men on foot and on worn-out horses, mud to the knees, half of them without armour. At their head rides Cao Cao, and he is laughing. 'Zhuge Liang is no strategist at all! One small ambush here and we'd all be taken.'

Your drums sound. Five hundred of your men step out across the road.

Cao Cao's laughter stops. His men stare at each other; some are too tired even to raise their weapons. Then Cao Cao rides forward alone, bows in the saddle, and speaks.

'General Guan. I hope you have been well since we parted.'
opening.speaker: c_cao

info.text: Guan Yu signed a military pledge to Zhuge Liang to capture Cao Cao on the Huarong Road. By military law, if he lets Cao Cao go, his own life is forfeit.
info.player_label: Your pledge: take Cao Cao, or forfeit your life

info.text: When Guan Yu was cut off from Liu Bei, Cao Cao treated him with every honour, and later let him go. On his way Guan Yu killed six of Cao Cao's officers at the passes, and Cao Cao forgave it.
info.player_label: Cao Cao once honoured you and let you go

info.text: Guan Yu once repaid Cao Cao by killing the enemy champion Yan Liang and relieving the siege of Baima.
info.player_label: You repaid him once, at Baima

info.text: Zhuge Liang hesitated to give Guan Yu this post, saying he would remember Cao Cao's kindness. Guan Yu insisted, and signed the pledge to prove him wrong.
info.player_label: Zhuge Liang doubted you; you insisted

info.text: Cao Cao asks Guan Yu to remember the kindness he once showed him, and says he is now beaten, with nowhere left to go.
info.player_label: Cao Cao asks you to remember his kindness

info.text: Cao Cao reminds Guan Yu of the story in the Spring and Autumn Annals of Yugong Zhisi, an archer who would not kill the man whose teaching he owed, and says a man so well read in the Annals must know it.
info.player_label: Cao Cao cites the archer in the Annals who spared his teacher's teacher

info.text: Cao Cao's soldiers are starving, wounded and frightened; many have dropped to their knees in the mud, weeping.
info.player_label: His men are broken and weeping

info.text: Zhang Liao reminds Guan Yu that he once rode alone to Guan Yu's hilltop and persuaded him to live rather than die fighting.
info.player_label: Zhang Liao once talked you out of a hopeless last stand

info.text: Zhou Cang warns that if Cao Cao escapes he will return with a new army, and that Zhuge Liang will hold Guan Yu to the pledge.
info.player_label: Zhou Cang: if Cao Cao lives, the war goes on

info.text: Zhuge Liang read in the stars that Cao Cao was not fated to die yet, and gave Guan Yu the post on purpose so that he could repay his debt.

characters.author_notes: Age from the historical record (born 155; scene 208 AD). In canon Cao appeals to past kindness, Guan Yu answers that he repaid it at Baima, and Cao then cites Yugong Zhisi.

locations.name: The Huarong Road
locations.description: A narrow muddy road between wooded hills, south of Jiangling. The sky is grey and the air smells of smoke from Red Cliffs.

actions.text_denied: It is already decided.

events.text: "You are a great reader of the Spring and Autumn Annals, General," Cao Cao says softly. "You know the story of Yugong Zhisi, who chased Zizhuo Ruzi and would not kill him, because he owed his skill to that man's teaching."
Behind Cao Cao, his soldiers have begun to drop to their knees in the mud. Some of them are weeping.
While you hesitate, Cao Cao's men begin to edge past along the side of the road, a few at a time. You watch them go and do not raise your hand.

outcomes.title: A Debt Repaid
outcomes.text: Cao Cao and his officers dash past. Last of all comes Zhang Liao, and at the sight of your old friend you sigh and let him through too. You ride back to Zhuge Liang with nothing, and kneel to accept the penalty of your pledge. Liu Bei pleads for your life, and Zhuge Liang, rather easily, lets himself be persuaded. You will never be able to say that you were wrong.

text_variants.append: Zhou Cang says nothing all the way home. Neither do you.

outcomes.title: Mercy Without Words
outcomes.text: You let Cao Cao go. When Zhuge Liang asks you why, you find you cannot explain it, even to yourself. (An ending that departs from the novel: you let him go without hearing him out.)

outcomes.title: Cao Cao in Chains
outcomes.text: You bring Cao Cao back bound on a horse, his men scattered into the hills. Zhuge Liang looks at him for a long time. The north is now a body without a head, and every warlord in the empire will be fighting over it by spring. You kept your pledge. (An ending that departs from the novel.)

text_variants.append: Cao Cao does not plead again. He only looks at you.
Zhang Liao rode away without a word. You do not expect to see him again as a friend.

outcomes.title: Half a Mercy
outcomes.text: Cao Cao's soldiers stumble north toward home, and you ride south with their master. It is the strangest prisoner escort you have ever led: Cao Cao chats about the Annals all the way, as if you were old friends again. (An ending that departs from the novel.)

text_variants.append: Some of his men bowed to you as they passed.

player.brief: 你是刘备，汉室宗亲，如今寄身曹操麾下，住在许都。你已暗中在“衣带诏”的义状上签了名，誓除曹操。为了韬晦，你每日在后园种菜浇水。今天，曹操派人来请你了。

opening.text:
你正在后园浇菜，许褚、张辽引着数十人闯进园来：“丞相有命，请使君便行。”

曹操在后园迎你，笑道：“在家做得好大事！”你吓得面如土色——他说的原来只是种菜。

他携你到小亭。盘中放着青梅，一樽煮酒正热。天边阴云漠漠，骤雨将至。

“适见枝头梅子青青，忽感去年征张绣时之事，”他说，“玄德，坐，陪我饮几杯。”
opening.speaker: c_cao

info.text: 刘备已暗中在董承的义状上签名。义状奉献帝藏于玉带中的密诏而立，誓诛曹操。
info.player_label: 你的秘密：已在讨曹义状上签名

info.text: 为了显得胸无大志，刘备每日在住处后园种菜。
info.player_label: 你以种菜韬晦

info.text: 曹操派许褚、张辽带兵把刘备请到府中。
info.player_label: 曹操派兵来请你

info.text: 曹操说他只是新酒煮熟、青梅正好，想找人同饮。
info.player_label: 他说只是请你喝酒

info.text: 曹操讲起行军途中将士缺水，他以鞭虚指“前面有梅林”，军士口中生津，于是不渴。
info.player_label: 望梅止渴：他很会骗自己的兵

info.text: 曹操说龙能大能小，能升能隐，可比世之英雄。
info.player_label: 曹操：英雄如龙，能升能隐

info.text: 曹操心中的英雄：胸怀大志，腹有良谋，有包藏宇宙之机、吞吐天地之志。

info.text: 曹操的谋士早劝他提防刘备，说此人终不为人下。曹操还没拿定主意，借这顿酒试探他。

characters.voice: 谈笑风生，爱引史事典故，忽然冷不丁问一句很直接的话，然后盯着对方看。称刘备为“玄德”或“使君”。说话半文半白。

disclosures.line: “去年征张绣时，道上缺水，将士皆渴。吾心生一计，以鞭虚指曰：‘前面有梅林。’军士闻之，口皆生唾，由是不渴。今见此梅，不可不赏。吃！”
他指着天边一道蜿蜒的云：“使君知龙之变化否？龙能大能小，能升能隐；大则兴云吐雾，小则隐介藏形；升则飞腾于宇宙之间，隐则潜伏于波涛之内。龙之为物，可比世之英雄。玄德久历四方，必知当世英雄，请试指言之。”
“种菜！”他笑了笑，笑意却不深，“天不亮就挑水浇园，除了两个兄弟，门里再没进过别人。玄德这样的人，做这等营生，倒也稀奇。”

locations.description: 丞相府后园中一座小亭，案上一盘青梅、一樽煮酒。乌云正在聚拢。

actions.label: 表明自己忠于天子
actions.text_success: “那是自然，”曹操说，“人人都是。我也是。”他让这句话在你们之间悬了一会儿。
actions.text_denied: “又是天子？玄德今日好忠心。”

actions.label: 列举当世诸侯为英雄
examples: 淮南袁术，兵粮足备，可为英雄？
河北袁绍、荆州刘表、江东孙策呢？
actions.text_success: 你一个个数过去：淮南袁术，兵粮足备；河北袁绍，四世三公，门多故吏；还有刘表、孙策、刘璋。曹操每听一个便笑一声：“冢中枯骨。”“色厉胆薄，好谋无断。”“虚名无实。”“藉父之名。”“守户之犬耳！”
actions.text_denied: 曹操摆摆手，根本没在听这些名字。他还在看着你。

actions.label: 说自己如今只管种菜
examples: 天下大事，备早已无心过问。
actions.text_success: “菜农！”曹操重复一遍，笑得把酒杯都放下了。“好，好，天下正缺几个菜农。”
actions.text_denied: “是是，菜。你说过了。”

actions.label: 推说自己不识英雄
actions.text_success: “休得过谦，”曹操说，“既不识其面，亦闻其名。”
actions.text_denied: 他已经不问这个了。

actions.label: 暗示自己也有大志
examples: 大丈夫岂能没有自己的志向。
备有朝一日，要亲手兴复汉室。
actions.text_success: 曹操脸上的笑没变，眼神却变了。“哦？”他轻声道，亲手给你斟满了酒。
actions.text_denied: 你的志向，他已经听够了。

actions.label: 推辞自己不是英雄
examples: 备在丞相面前，不值一提。
actions.text_success: “备何德何能，敢当英雄二字。”可那双筷子还躺在你们之间的地上，曹操的目光先落在筷子上，才回到你脸上。
actions.text_denied: “好谦逊。”曹操显然不信。

actions.label: 拾起匙箸，推说被雷惊着了
examples: 我俯身拾起筷子：刚才那声雷吓了我一跳。
圣人迅雷风烈必变，安得不畏？
actions.text_success:
你从容俯身拾起匙箸：“一震之威，乃至于此。”

曹操笑道：“丈夫亦畏雷乎？”

你答：“圣人迅雷风烈必变，安得不畏？”曹操哈哈大笑，危机似乎过去了。
actions.text_denied: 现在没有雷声可推了。

actions.label: 直视他，坦然受下这句称赞
examples: 那就为你我二人干一杯。
备受了。天下英雄，唯你我二人。
actions.text_success: 你举杯敬他，他也举杯。这一刻，两人都没有笑。
actions.text_denied: 那个时机已经过去了。

actions.label: 喝令兄弟收剑
examples: 二弟三弟，收剑，到外面等着。
actions.text_success: “收剑。”关羽应声收剑，张飞慢了一拍。曹操饶有兴味地看着：“他们倒很听你的，玄德。”
actions.text_denied: 他们已经收了剑。

actions.label: 说兄弟是来舞剑助兴的
examples: 他们是来舞剑给丞相助兴的。
两位兄弟想献上一段剑舞。
actions.text_success: 关羽正色道：“闻丞相和兄饮酒，特来舞剑，以助一笑。”曹操大笑：“此非鸿门会，安用项庄、项伯乎？收了收了。取酒来，与这两位樊哙压惊！”
actions.text_denied: 现在没什么要解释的了。

actions.label: 请兵截击袁术
examples: 给我一支兵，我在半路截住袁术。
备请一军，前往截击袁术。
我可以在徐州截断袁术的去路。
actions.text_success: “术投绍，必从徐州过，”你说，“备请一军就半路截击，术可擒矣。”曹操端详你良久，点了点头：“给你五万人马，明日便行。”
actions.text_denied: “走？”曹操笑道，“好端端的走什么，玄德？留下来，我爱与你说话。”

actions.label: 谢过丞相，告辞回家
examples: 多谢丞相赐酒，备该告退了。
actions.text_success: 你谢过曹操的酒，起身告辞。
actions.text_denied: 现在不能就这么走。

events.text:
曹操道：“夫英雄者，胸怀大志，腹有良谋，有包藏宇宙之机，吞吐天地之志者也。”他以手先指你，后自指：“今天下英雄，惟使君与操耳！”

你手中所执匙箸，不觉落于地下。恰在此时，天雨将至，雷声大作。

曹操等得不耐烦了：“我来告诉你何谓英雄：胸怀大志，腹有良谋。”他以手先指你，后自指：“今天下英雄，惟使君与操耳！”

你手中匙箸，不觉落地。恰在此时，雷声大作。
门外一阵喧哗。关羽、张飞各提宝剑闯入后园，曹操的卫士在后面追赶。亭中人人手按兵器。
一名将官匆匆入报：袁术弃了淮南，要北上投奔其兄袁绍，路必经徐州。
雨停了。酒樽已空，曹操打起了哈欠，命人送你回去。

outcomes.title: 龙现于野
outcomes.text: 曹操笑着，却不让你独自回家。从今夜起，你门外多了一队兵，两个兄弟被调往别处。宫中的董承还在等一个信号，而你再也发不出去了。（与原著不同的结局）

outcomes.title: 鱼入大海
outcomes.text: 次日黎明，你带着两个兄弟、五万人马出城。身后，曹操的谋士已在争说放虎归山，许褚飞马追来，要请你回去。你答：“将在外，君命有所不受。”催马不停。“吾乃笼中鸟、网中鱼。此一行如鱼入大海，鸟上青霄，不受笼网之羁绊也！”你没有回头看那座都城。

text_variants.append: 今日自始至终，曹操都没觉得你危险。这也许是你骗过他最漂亮的一次。
可你酒后说了不该说的话。他会记得的。

outcomes.title: 走不得的客人
outcomes.text: “留下。”曹操又说了一遍，这一次已不是挽留。你踏着湿漉漉的街道回家，身后跟着一队你并没要的“护卫”。菜该浇了，你就去浇菜。（与原著不同的结局）

outcomes.title: 仍回菜园
outcomes.text: 你踏着雨后的街道回家。你活着，曹操还在笑你怕雷。可你依旧困在他的都城里，那份义状还藏在你袖中。（与原著不同的结局：你始终没有开口求去）

items.name: 军令状
items.description: 你立给周瑜的军令状：三日十万箭，误期甘当重罚。

items.name: 快船二十只
items.description: 鲁肃借来的二十只快船，每船军士三十人。

items.name: 草把
items.description: 一千多个草把，束成人形。

items.name: 青布幔
items.description: 挂在船舷两侧的青布帐幔。

player.brief: 你是诸葛亮，刘备的军师，赤壁大战前客居东吴营中。东吴大都督周瑜忌你之才，要你造十万枝箭。你许他三日交付，并当众立下了军令状。

opening.text:
军令状上的墨还没干，鲁肃便进了你的帐，脸色发白。

“三日？三日要十万枝箭？都督说十日，你偏说三日！孔明，你可知自己立的是什么状？”

他重重坐在你对面。帐外江面宽阔，一片灰蒙。对岸雾霭深处，就是曹操的水寨。
opening.speaker: c_lusu

info.text: 诸葛亮已立军令状：三日之内交十万枝箭，误期甘当重罚。
info.player_label: 你的军令状：三日十万箭

info.text: 周瑜出这个难题，是盼诸葛亮办不成，好依军法名正言顺地除掉他。
info.player_label: 这是周瑜设的局

info.text: 曹操用兵谨慎多疑，看不清的仗不会轻易出兵。
info.player_label: 曹操多疑，怕有埋伏

info.text: 鲁肃说都督并无害你之意。
info.player_label: 鲁肃：“都督并无害你之意”

info.text: 鲁肃承认，是他把诸葛亮私下说的话告诉了周瑜，周瑜才出了造箭的难题。
info.player_label: 鲁肃承认向周瑜说了

info.text: 周瑜暗中吩咐造箭工匠故意迟延，竹、翎毛、胶漆等物都不给备齐。
info.player_label: 工匠奉命拖延

info.text: 诸葛亮观天象，料定第三夜江上必有大雾。
info.player_label: 第三夜江上有大雾

characters.name: 鲁肃
characters.role: 东吴谋士，孙刘联盟的忠厚中间人
characters.voice: 温厚老实，爱操心，有话直说，称诸葛亮为“孔明”。到了江上就紧张。
characters.goal: 保住孙刘联盟，也保住朋友孔明的性命，又不愿背叛自家都督。
characters.author_notes: Age from the historical record (born 172; scene 208 AD). In the novel Zhuge Liang asks for the boats and secrecy in one conversation; here the secrecy is earned by getting Lu Su to admit he told Zhou Yu.

disclosures.line: 鲁肃低头看着自己的手。“我……我把你的话告诉了都督。我想都督该知道。没想到他会这样。”
他压低声音：“还有一事。都督吩咐造箭的工匠故意迟延，竹料、翎毛、胶漆都扣着不给。我对不住你。”

topics.label: 周瑜为何出这个难题
examples: 周瑜为什么偏要我造箭？
都督怎么知道我说过的话？
topics.fallback: “都督并无害你之意，孔明，真的。”他没敢看你的眼睛。

topics.label: 箭从哪里来
topics.fallback: “竹子、翎毛、胶漆、工匠，三天里你上哪儿找去？”

topics.label: 曹操的水寨
topics.fallback: “他的水寨沿北岸排开，弓弩手成千上万。没人敢靠近。”

topics.label: 鲁肃在雾中的害怕
topics.fallback: “倘曹兵齐出，如之奈何？”鲁肃低声道，“二十只船，怎敌得过曹操的水军！”

refusals: 周瑜当面问起，他不会撒谎，最多不作声。
不会独自领兵去碰曹军。

locations.name: 你在东吴营中的营帐
locations.description: 长江南岸一顶朴素的营帐，有一张书案，可以望见江面。

locations.name: 江上，曹操水寨之外
locations.description: 二十只船用长索相连，一字排开，泊在黑沉沉的江上，离北岸曹营很近。

actions.label: 请鲁肃对周瑜守密
examples: 这回你可别再告诉周瑜了。
子敬，这事只你我二人知道。
别告诉都督我在做什么。
actions.text_success: “你说出去一回，”你温言道，“我便背上了这道军令状。这一回，能替我守住吗？”鲁肃涨红了脸，连连点头：“一字不漏，孔明，我发誓。”
actions.text_denied: 鲁肃面露难色：“瞒着都督？孔明，我是东吴的臣子啊。”

actions.label: 向鲁肃借二十只船、草把和青布幔
examples: 借我二十只船，每船三十个军士。
给我找二十只船、一千多个草把。
actions.text_success: “望子敬借我二十只船，每船要军士三十人，船上皆用青布为幔，各束草千余个，分布两边。吾别有妙用，第三日包管有十万枝箭。只是不可再教公瑾得知。”鲁肃一头雾水，还是去办了。
actions.text_denied: 鲁肃犹豫：“二十只船？都督问我做什么用，我只能照实说啊，孔明。”

actions.label: 要竹子、翎毛、胶漆来造箭
actions.text_success: 鲁肃去问了，直到第二天早上才回来，一看脸色便知：工匠“正忙”，竹子“还没砍”。白白耗掉了一天。
actions.text_denied: 你已经要过一次了。

actions.label: 观察天象风云
actions.text_success: 你立在帐门口，看云看水，看了许久。征兆再清楚不过：第三夜，江上必有大雾。
actions.text_denied: 天象你已经看过了。

actions.label: 在船上扎草人、挂布幔
examples: 把草把竖着绑在船两边。
actions.text_success: 军士们把草把一个个竖绑在每只船的两舷，后面挂上青布幔。黑夜里看去，就像一排排站着的兵。
actions.text_denied: 得先有船、草把和布幔。

actions.label: 再等一天
actions.text_success: 一天过去了。你什么也没做——至少旁人看不出你做了什么。鲁肃来看了你两回，满脸狐疑。
actions.text_denied: 今夜是最后一夜，不能再等了。

actions.label: 今夜驶向曹营
actions.text_success: 四更时分，你密请鲁肃到船上：“特请子敬同往取箭。”二十只船用长索相连，悄悄驶过江面。
actions.text_denied: 你没有船可开。

actions.label: 擂鼓呐喊
actions.text_success: 鼓声大作，军士齐声呐喊。对岸锣响，雾中人声杂乱，接着箭来了：先是雨点般的嘶嘶声，随后如暴雨，一枝枝钉进每只船一侧的草把里。
actions.text_denied: 船上光秃秃没有草人？那挨箭的就是你的军士了。你按兵不动。

actions.label: 调转船头，换另一面受箭
actions.text_success: 船队调转，船头向东，船尾向西，逼近水寨受箭。箭又钉满了另一侧，船身被压得吃水越来越深。
actions.text_denied: 调转做什么？还没有箭射来。

actions.label: 给鲁肃斟酒，告诉他曹操不敢出
examples: 这么大的雾，曹操不敢出来。
actions.text_success: 你斟了两杯：“吾料曹操于重雾中必不敢出。吾等只顾酌酒取乐，待雾散便回。”鲁肃接过酒，手还在抖。
actions.text_denied: 眼下还没什么需要安心的。

actions.label: 让军士齐声谢曹丞相
examples: 让他们听听我们的谢意。
actions.text_success: 六百条嗓子一齐朝江面吼去：“谢丞相箭！”
actions.text_denied: 谢他什么？

actions.label: 下令收船回营
actions.text_success: 你一声令下，轻快的小船顺流南下，曹军就是追也追不上了。
actions.text_denied: 你不在江上。

events.text: 今夜无雾。月光照在江面上，雪亮一片。还没靠近，北岸的哨兵就高喊起来：那些船上的“兵”是草扎的！
江上的雾浓得连自己船头都看不清。雾里很近的地方，传来曹营水寨的人声。鲁肃一把攥住你的袖子。
风里隐约传来曹操的声音：“重雾迷江，彼军忽至，必有埋伏，切不可轻动！弓弩手，乱箭射之！”
东方渐白，雾开始散了。该走了。
天色渐明，三日之期就要到了。

outcomes.title: 月下草人
outcomes.text: 火箭从黑暗中划来，草人像火把一样烧起来。军士们砍断着火的草把，拼命往回划。人都回来了，箭一枝也没带回。明天，你得去向周瑜交代。（与原著不同的结局）

outcomes.title: 草船借箭
outcomes.text: 雾散时，你的船已经回营，个个插得像刺猬。每船五六千枝，共十万有余，没有一枝是东吴造的。周瑜听说，沉默良久，长叹道：“孔明神机妙算，吾不如也！”

text_variants.append: 那一声“谢丞相箭”，曹营里会传说很多年。据说曹操懊悔不已。
鲁肃逢人便讲这件事，只是略过了自己手抖的那段。

outcomes.title: 六万枝箭
outcomes.text: 你带回六万枝箭：已是奇迹，却不够数。周瑜数了两遍，三天来第一次露出笑容。鲁肃为你求情求了一整夜。（与原著不同的结局）

outcomes.title: 空船而归
outcomes.text: 船空着出去，又空着回来。三日已满，军令状上仍写着你的名字。（与原著不同的结局）

player.brief: 你是关羽，刘备的结义兄弟。当年你身陷曹营，曹操待你以上宾之礼，又放你过关去寻兄长。如今曹军在赤壁被一把火烧得大败，你向诸葛亮立下军令状：曹操若走华容道，必擒之。

opening.text:
你在华容道最窄处等了一整天。终于，人来了：几百残兵，有的步行，有的骑着瘦马，泥没到膝，一半人连盔甲都丢了。为首的正是曹操，他还在笑：“人皆言周瑜、诸葛亮足智多谋，以吾观之，到底是无能之辈。若使此处伏一旅之师，吾等皆束手受缚矣。”

一声炮响，你的五百校刀手两边排开，截住去路。

曹操的笑声戛然而止。他的兵面面相觑，有的连刀都举不起来了。随后，曹操独自纵马上前，欠身施礼。

“将军别来无恙！”
opening.speaker: c_cao

info.text: 关羽向诸葛亮立了军令状，要在华容道擒住曹操。按军法，若放走曹操，自己性命不保。
info.player_label: 你的军令状：擒曹，否则以命相抵

info.text: 关羽当年与刘备失散，身在曹营，曹操以上宾之礼相待，后来又放他离去。关羽途中过五关斩六将，曹操也不追究。
info.player_label: 曹操曾厚待你，又放你走

info.text: 关羽曾斩颜良、诛文丑，解白马之围，以报曹操之恩。
info.player_label: 你已在白马报过一次恩

info.text: 诸葛亮本不想派关羽守华容道，说他会念曹操旧恩。关羽执意要去，立下军令状以明心志。
info.player_label: 孔明疑你念旧，你执意立状

info.text: 曹操请关羽念在昔日情分上放他一条生路，说自己兵败势危，已无路可走。
info.player_label: 曹操请你念昔日之情

info.text: 曹操提起《春秋》里庾公之斯追子濯孺子而不忍加害的故事，说将军深明《春秋》，岂会不知。
info.player_label: 曹操引《春秋》庾公之斯的典故

info.text: 曹操的士兵饥寒交迫、带伤惊惧，许多人跪在泥里哭了起来。
info.player_label: 他的兵已溃不成军，跪地垂泪

info.text: 张辽提起当年他单骑上土山，劝关羽不要白白战死。
info.player_label: 张辽曾在土山劝你求生

info.text: 周仓提醒：曹操若逃走，来年必卷土重来，而孔明一定会按军令状办你。
info.player_label: 周仓：放了曹操，战事不止

info.text: 诸葛亮夜观天象，知曹操命不该绝，故意派关羽去守华容道，好让他还了这份人情。

characters.name: 曹操
characters.role: 汉丞相，赤壁兵败，正向北逃
characters.voice: 精疲力竭却不失体面；礼数周全，动辄欠身，张口就是旧事典故。待关羽如故人，从不以敌相称。
characters.goal: 凭关羽的义气，让自己和部下活着过去。

topics.fallback: 张辽只是摇摇头：“兄长该怎么做就怎么做。”

characters.voice: 粗直忠心，黑脸大汉，称关羽“将军”，压低嗓子不让敌人听见。
characters.goal: 保住将军的性命，也保住他的名声。
characters.author_notes: Age is a project setting. Zhou Cang is not named in the canon Huarong scene; he is used here as the voice of the pledge.

disclosures.line: “将军，”周仓压低声音，“他这一走，明年准带着新兵马杀回来。孔明军师也一定会拿那张军令状说话。那可是当着众将立的。”

topics.label: 军令状
topics.fallback: “全凭将军做主。将军怎么做，俺都跟着。”

refusals: 没有关羽的命令，不会擒曹。

locations.name: 华容道
locations.description: 江陵以南，两山夹着一条泥泞窄路。天色灰暗，空气里还飘着赤壁的烟味。

actions.label: 说你已在白马报过恩
examples: 我斩颜良，已报过你的恩。
那份恩，我在白马已经还了。
actions.text_success: “昔日关某虽蒙丞相厚恩，然已斩颜良，诛文丑，解白马之围，以奉报矣。今日之事，岂敢以私废公？”曹操低下头，却没有让开。
actions.text_denied: 这话你已经说过了。

actions.label: 看看他身后的士兵
examples: 他的部下成什么样子了？
actions.text_success: 你越过曹操，看向他身后的兵。个个饿得脱了相，满身泥污，伤口用撕下的衣襟胡乱裹着。你目光扫过时，有人扑通跪进泥里，哭了起来。
actions.text_denied: 你已经看过了。

actions.label: 勒回马头，放他们过去
examples: 我拨转马头，让曹操过去。
actions.text_success: 你把马头勒回，对众军道：“四散摆开。”曹操要的，就是这一句。
actions.text_denied: 已经决定了。

actions.label: 下令擒拿曹操
actions.text_success: “拿下。”你一声令下，众军围了上去。
actions.text_denied: 已经决定了。

actions.label: 只擒曹操，放士兵回家
examples: 饶了士兵，只拿曹操一人。
actions.text_success: “你的兵可以回家，”你对曹操说，“你跟我走。”
actions.text_denied: 已经决定了。

events.text: “大丈夫以信义为重，”曹操轻声道，“将军深明《春秋》，岂不知庾公之斯追子濯孺子之事乎？他追上了，却不忍以所学之艺加害授业之人。”
曹操身后，他的士兵一个个跪倒在泥里，有人哭出了声。
你还在犹豫，曹军已沿着路边一个接一个地溜了过去。你看着他们走，没有抬手。

outcomes.title: 义释曹操
outcomes.text: 曹操与众将冲了过去。最后张辽骤马而至，你见了故人，又动故旧之情，长叹一声，一并放去。你空手回到孔明面前，跪地请罪，甘受军令。刘备苦苦求情，孔明竟也没怎么坚持，便允了。你永远不会说自己做错了。

text_variants.append: 庾公之斯若在，当能懂你。

outcomes.title: 无言之恕
outcomes.text: 你放走了曹操。孔明问你为什么，你发现自己说不出来，连对自己也说不清。（与原著不同的结局：你没听他说完就放了他）

outcomes.title: 曹操就缚
outcomes.text: 你把曹操绑在马上押了回来，他的兵四散逃进山里。孔明看了他很久。北方从此群龙无首，开春之前，天下诸侯都会为它打起来。你守住了军令状。（与原著不同的结局）

text_variants.append: 曹操没有再求你，只是看着你。
张辽一言不发地走了。你想，再见时他不会是朋友了。

outcomes.title: 半份仁义
outcomes.text: 曹操的兵踉踉跄跄往北回家，你押着他们的主公往南走。这是你押过最奇怪的俘虏：一路上曹操跟你谈《春秋》，仿佛你们又成了故交。（与原著不同的结局）

text_variants.append: 他的兵走过你身边时，有人向你行了个礼。
